introHeading: The green screen booth for Queens' catering-hall weddings and Sweet Sixteens
introParas: Queens brings us the biggest guest lists of any borough we cover — multigenerational weddings, Sweet Sixteens that fill an entire catering hall, and company parties in Long Island City spaces with the ceiling height to match. A green screen booth handles that scale differently than a fixed backdrop would: because the scene lives in software, we can swap it mid-event without touching a single prop — a formal set behind the family portraits in the first hour, something louder once the dance floor fills in. Custom props built to match whatever background you've chosen keep a themed Sweet Sixteen shot from feeling generic, rather than a birthday girl holding a stock prop borrowed from another party.

With guest counts that size, throughput is the real design problem. We often pair the green screen booth with a roaming attendant so the line at the main setup never becomes the whole night's activity — the roamer works the seated tables and the cocktail hour while the booth keeps its own queue moving with stills, GIFs and boomerangs.

Catering halls in Astoria, Flushing and Forest Hills are where we set this up most often, and the taller ceilings in Long Island City's converted event spaces give us room for a larger backdrop screen when a corporate client wants something more theatrical. Queens is a standard service area with no surprise fees — travel is quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book, covering Jamaica and Ridgewood the same as anywhere closer in.

faqHeading: Green Screen Booth in Queens — FAQ

faqs.q: Can the background change partway through our Queens reception?
faqs.a: Yes. Because the scene is built in software rather than physically installed, our attendant can switch it during the event — a formal look for the early hours, something different once the dancing starts.

faqs.q: Do you recommend pairing the green screen booth with a roaming attendant for a large guest list?
faqs.a: For catering-hall guest counts, often yes. The roamer covers the seated tables and cocktail hour so nobody spends the whole reception waiting in one line, while the main booth keeps its own queue moving.

faqs.q: How far ahead do you need the custom background designed for a Sweet Sixteen theme?
faqs.a: At least two weeks for a fully custom build gives our design team time to build it and get your sign-off. A simpler swap can turn around faster — ask and we'll tell you what's realistic for your date.

faqs.q: Does the taller ceiling in a Long Island City venue change the setup?
faqs.a: It gives us more room, not less work — the extra height lets us build a larger backdrop screen when an event calls for something more theatrical, which corporate clients in LIC often want.

faqs.q: How much floor space does the green screen booth need in a catering hall?
faqs.a: Optimal setup is 10ft x 10ft. We can compress to a minimum of 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance in a tighter room, and we need a standard 110V, 5-amp, 3-prong outlet within 15 feet.

faqs.q: Is there a travel fee for Queens events?
faqs.a: Queens is a standard service area with no surprise fees. We quote travel from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with the rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the booth for the full length of your rental — managing background swaps, keeping props organized, and helping guests through a busy catering-hall crowd.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance for a catering hall that requires a COI?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $2 million insurance policy. If your venue needs a certificate naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we'll send it over.
